text:
max: quick heads-up — we ran the sparse-batcher + token-compression canary on a small dedicated pool this morning. numbers look good, rolling notes below. :party-parrot:

sophia: awesome — TL;DR numbers?

max: short summary: p50 latency down ~18%, p99 roughly flat, token cost down ~27% for generation workloads. throughput up ~12% on mixed-seq.

anita: do you have the bench output? paste logs pls.

max: pasted below (canary pool: g5.2x, model: rw-7b-v3-econ):

```
CANARY BENCH — 2026-03-22 09:12 UTC
Model: rw-7b-v3-econ
Traffic profile: 60% gen, 40% chat
Before (baseline): p50=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=310ms, tps=950 tokens/s, cost= $0.012 / 1k tokens
After (sparse-batcher + token-compression): p50=59ms, p95=208ms, p99=295ms, tps=1064 tokens/s, cost= $0.00875 / 1k tokens
Delta: p50 -18.1%, p99 -4.8%, throughput +12%, unit-cost -27.1%
CPU offload diff: host cpu reduced ~20% on canary nodes
Important: small increase in token-encoding CPU during decode window, but overall net win.
```

dave: nice. where did we see p99 improvements — not huge, but cost drop is great.

max: p99 improved a bit because compression reduces memory pressure which helps microbatch packing consistency. main wins are p50 and cost.

infra-bot: canary health: all checks green (latency, error-rate, memory) — 6/6 passing.

sophia: any edge cases? long-seq or high-context convs?

max: long-seq (>2k) sees marginal decode CPU spike; flagged under 0.5% of requests in canary. plan: disable compression for requests with seq_len>2500 via routing rule.

anita: rollout plan?

max: propose: increase canary to 25% today, 50% tomorrow morning if no regressions, full by EOD tomorrow. flags: sparse_batcher.enable=true, compression.level=2, compression.seq_threshold=2500.

marcus: do we need to update the dedicated pricing calc? this will change unit economics for reserved customers.

sophia: ops: can we surface cost delta in console per-route? would be helpful for customers before full flip.

ops-bot: created ticket: INF-4821 "Expose sparse-batcher cost delta in console per-route" — assignee: anita. link: https://rwinf.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821

anita: assigned, will prototype a delta card on the model dashboard (est 2d).

dave: any rollout kill-switch?

max: yes — rollback via configservice: set sparse_batcher.enable=false for the pool, or hit the per-pool toggle in console (Route -> Advanced -> Runtime Flags). quick curl to flip: 

```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/internal/pools/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"pool":"gd-dedicated-small","flags":{"sparse_batcher.enable":false}}'
```

sophia: loving the cost numbers. can we add a short blurb for the daily stand and the release notes?

max: will post a 1-paragraph blurb in releases channel + add bench link. thumbs if you want me to announce to #all-hands after full rollout. :thumbsup:

marcus: :thumbsup: from infra — great work.

anita: quick ask — add a canary alert for seq_len regressions ( >2k ) so we catch any customer-visible slowdowns early.

max: noted, adding alert w/ 15min window.

infra-bot: rollout metrics link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/canaries/sparse-batcher-2923456789

sophia: thanks team. short, focused, and measurable win. :tada:
